sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's is a qualifying degree route, provided it is completed before enrollment and the
mathematical preparation requirement is met: advanced analysis, abstract algebra and linear algebra; fuller
algebra/analysis sequences and topology preferred, complex variables expected for PhD. Research is not a
prerequisite. F-1 status does not itself establish academic eligibility. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD in GradApp, prepare records and upper-division mathematics list, request recent
letters, and use the international fee-waiver prescreen before paying if desired. No supervisor commitment is
listed. After admission, international financial/passport evidence and immigration processing are separate;
June 1 is an administrative departmental recommendation deadline, not the Math application deadline. [s1] [s3]
[s11] [s15]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement listed. Douglas Ulmer explicitly invites discussion of graduate projects on his
homepage. Contact relevant faculty using current department profiles, asking about Fall 2027 supervision;
directory presence does not guarantee availability. [s1] [s16] [s22]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
GradApp: create profile; upload PDFs; complete fee payment, review, and final Submit. Successful submission
generates email; processing checklist tracks progress. Letters and decisions are handled through the portal,
but several Math-specific referee controls are not publicly documented. [s3] [s12]

Math page explicitly publishes January 10, 2027 and late-October opening. Funding, some English wording and
scholarship timetables have older bases; distinguish those from the current admission deadline. [s1] [s5] [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Central doctoral admission: TOEFL iBT 4.0 on the new scale (old scale 79), IELTS 7.0 with each component 6.0,
or listed alternatives including PTE 60. TOEFL Essentials is not a doctoral admission option. Scores must be
within two years of enrollment. Math's older TOEFL 79 wording predates the new scale. TA qualification is
separate: new TOEFL speaking 5.0/old 24, IELTS speaking 7.5, or another approved teaching-language route; a
US degree does not automatically waive it. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US bachelor's qualifies for the admission English exemption. If applying before degree completion,
the central rule requires two years full-time study and 48 graded upper-division semester units within the
specified two-year window; have Arizona verify how UChicago quarter units and upper-division coursework
satisfy this. Admission waiver does not waive TA speaking qualification. [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; submit if helpful. Upload a copy or send ETS results to institution 4832, mathematics department
0703. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; accepted if it adds useful evidence. No required score threshold published. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
University-wide AY 2026-27 minimum for a 0.50-FTE graduate assistant is USD 25,654 for nine months;
fiscal-year minimum USD 33,350 is a distinct appointment basis. Neither is a published Fall 2027 Math offer.
Handbook's February 2026 table starts at USD 23,000 and is superseded by the later higher floor. At 0.50 FTE,
base tuition and individual student health premium are covered; mandatory/program/course fees are not
generally covered. University Fellows first year: USD 37,000 (15,000 fall + 15,000 spring + 7,000 summer),
base fall/spring tuition and health; year-two professional-development USD 500. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Handbook describes support after year three for two, possibly three more years subject to progress and
teaching; sixth-year support needs advisor/committee recommendation and beyond six is exceptional. A
guaranteed initial multi-year 2027 package was not located. University Fellows requires departmental support
in years 2-5, subject to performance and funds, with specified minimum support; first-year award is not the
ordinary TA stipend. [s5] [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students may pursue departmental assistantships subject to teaching-English and appointment
rules. University Fellows eligibility says any newly admitted qualifying doctoral student, without a citizenship
restriction. Graduate Access Fellowship explicitly targets domestic students and is not an F-1 funding route. [s1]
[s8] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Assistantship continuation requires satisfactory progress and teaching, at least six credits and GPA 3.0 under
handbook rules. First-year teaching load is four units per semester; later nine annually, plus training. University
Fellows requires full-time nine-credit enrollment, GPA 3.0, cohort participation, and normally no other paid
work in year one; exceptions require approval. [s5] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate standard TA application located. University Fellows requires department selection and nomination
(up to two nominees/program). Ask Math early whether it will nominate you; 2027 nomination date is
unpublished. [s1] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University Fellows; department awards for enrolled students, including teaching/research awards and some
later-stage university nominations. Math's scholarship page also lists citizenship- or institution-restricted
schemes; Arizona-undergraduate awards and domestic Graduate Access funding do not fit this UChicago F-1
profile. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 90 central graduate application fee, unless a qualifying program waiver applies; nonrefundable after
payment. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Math offers international applicants a free prescreen survey for possible fee waiver; apply through the linked
Qualtrics form before paying. Eligibility threshold, survey questions and 2027 cutoff are not publicly readable.
The separate broad domestic waiver is explicitly Fall 2026 and does not establish John's eligibility. Graduate
College does not provide a general waiver for everyone. [s1] [s4] [s11]

Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's is a qualifying degree route, provided it is completed before enrollment and the
mathematical preparation requirement is met: advanced analysis, abstract algebra and linear algebra; fuller
algebra/analysis sequences and topology preferred, complex variables expected for PhD. Research is not a
prerequisite. F-1 status does not itself establish academic eligibility. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD in GradApp, prepare records and upper-division mathematics list, request recent
letters, and use the international fee-waiver prescreen before paying if desired. No supervisor commitment is
listed. After admission, international financial/passport evidence and immigration processing are separate;
June 1 is an administrative departmental recommendation deadline, not the Math application deadline. [s1] [s3]
[s11] [s15]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement listed. Douglas Ulmer explicitly invites discussion of graduate projects on his
homepage. Contact relevant faculty using current department profiles, asking about Fall 2027 supervision;
directory presence does not guarantee availability. [s1] [s16] [s22]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
GradApp: create profile; upload PDFs; complete fee payment, review, and final Submit. Successful submission
generates email; processing checklist tracks progress. Letters and decisions are handled through the portal,
but several Math-specific referee controls are not publicly documented. [s3] [s12]

Central doctoral admission: TOEFL iBT 4.0 on the new scale (old scale 79), IELTS 7.0 with each component 6.0,

within two years of enrollment. Math's older TOEFL 79 wording predates the new scale. TA qualification is

US degree does not automatically waive it. [s1] [s2]

A completed US bachelor's qualifies for the admission English exemption. If applying before degree completion,
the central rule requires two years full-time study and 48 graded upper-division semester units within the
specified two-year window; have Arizona verify how UChicago quarter units and upper-division coursework
satisfy this. Admission waiver does not waive TA speaking qualification. [s2]

Amount and coverage [Conflict]
University-wide AY 2026-27 minimum for a 0.50-FTE graduate assistant is USD 25,654 for nine months;
fiscal-year minimum USD 33,350 is a distinct appointment basis. Neither is a published Fall 2027 Math offer.
Handbook's February 2026 table starts at USD 23,000 and is superseded by the later higher floor. At 0.50 FTE,
base tuition and individual student health premium are covered; mandatory/program/course fees are not
generally covered. University Fellows first year: USD 37,000 (15,000 fall + 15,000 spring + 7,000 summer),
base fall/spring tuition and health; year-two professional-development USD 500. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Handbook describes support after year three for two, possibly three more years subject to progress and
teaching; sixth-year support needs advisor/committee recommendation and beyond six is exceptional. A
guaranteed initial multi-year 2027 package was not located. University Fellows requires departmental support
in years 2-5, subject to performance and funds, with specified minimum support; first-year award is not the
ordinary TA stipend. [s5] [s9]

International students may pursue departmental assistantships subject to teaching-English and appointment
rules. University Fellows eligibility says any newly admitted qualifying doctoral student, without a citizenship
restriction. Graduate Access Fellowship explicitly targets domestic students and is not an F-1 funding route. [s1]

Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Assistantship continuation requires satisfactory progress and teaching, at least six credits and GPA 3.0 under
handbook rules. First-year teaching load is four units per semester; later nine annually, plus training. University
Fellows requires full-time nine-credit enrollment, GPA 3.0, cohort participation, and normally no other paid
work in year one; exceptions require approval. [s5] [s9]

No separate standard TA application located. University Fellows requires department selection and nomination
(up to two nominees/program). Ask Math early whether it will nominate you; 2027 nomination date is
unpublished. [s1] [s10]

University Fellows; department awards for enrolled students, including teaching/research awards and some
later-stage university nominations. Math's scholarship page also lists citizenship- or institution-restricted
schemes; Arizona-undergraduate awards and domestic Graduate Access funding do not fit this UChicago F-1
profile. [s8] [s9]

USD 90 central graduate application fee, unless a qualifying program waiver applies; nonrefundable after
payment. [s4]

Pay attention to
• Do not use the separate Applied Mathematics program's deadlines.
• Letters must be no more than one year old.
• International fee-waiver prescreen exists; ordinary domestic waiver does not apply.

area-roster names are not treated as ordinary 2027 advisers.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
UChicago bachelor's is a qualifying degree route, provided it is completed before enrollment and the
mathematical preparation requirement is met: advanced analysis, abstract algebra and linear algebra; fuller
algebra/analysis sequences and topology preferred, complex variables expected for PhD. Research is not a
prerequisite. F-1 status does not itself establish academic eligibility. [s1] [s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose Mathematics PhD in GradApp, prepare records and upper-division mathematics list, request recent
letters, and use the international fee-waiver prescreen before paying if desired. No supervisor commitment is
listed. After admission, international financial/passport evidence and immigration processing are separate;
June 1 is an administrative departmental recommendation deadline, not the Math application deadline. [s1] [s3]
[s11] [s15]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement listed. Douglas Ulmer explicitly invites discussion of graduate projects on his
homepage. Contact relevant faculty using current department profiles, asking about Fall 2027 supervision;
directory presence does not guarantee availability. [s1] [s16] [s22]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
GradApp: create profile; upload PDFs; complete fee payment, review, and final Submit. Successful submission
generates email; processing checklist tracks progress. Letters and decisions are handled through the portal,
but several Math-specific referee controls are not publicly documented. [s3] [s12]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Math page explicitly publishes January 10, 2027 and late-October opening. Funding, some English wording and
scholarship timetables have older bases; distinguish those from the current admission deadline. [s1] [s5] [s7]
[s10]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
January 10, 2027. Time zone/cutoff hour not published. Late applications may be possible only by contacting
the graduate office. [s1]

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
No separate 2027 Math funding date located; submit complete admission materials by January 10. University
Fellows departmental nomination dates are still Spring 2026: February 5, 2026, 11:59 p.m. MST; this is NOT a
2027 deadline. [s1] [s10]
Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Unresolved]
Treat January 10, 2027 as the complete-file target. No separate Math grace period or independently stated
receipt cutoff was found. Do not borrow another Arizona department's late-material policy. [s1] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Math admission/assistantship 2027 acceptance date not located. University Fellows page gives April 15 but its
dated recruitment timetable is Spring 2026; obtain the Fall 2027 offer deadline. [s10]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Central doctoral admission: TOEFL iBT 4.0 on the new scale (old scale 79), IELTS 7.0 with each component 6.0,
or listed alternatives including PTE 60. TOEFL Essentials is not a doctoral admission option. Scores must be
within two years of enrollment. Math's older TOEFL 79 wording predates the new scale. TA qualification is
separate: new TOEFL speaking 5.0/old 24, IELTS speaking 7.5, or another approved teaching-language route; a
US degree does not automatically waive it. [s1] [s2]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed US bachelor's qualifies for the admission English exemption. If applying before degree completion,
the central rule requires two years full-time study and 48 graded upper-division semester units within the
specified two-year window; have Arizona verify how UChicago quarter units and upper-division coursework
satisfy this. Admission waiver does not waive TA speaking qualification. [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; submit if helpful. Upload a copy or send ETS results to institution 4832, mathematics department
0703. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; accepted if it adds useful evidence. No required score threshold published. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload unofficial PDF transcripts for every prior college/university, plus degree certificates where applicable.
Official records are requested after admission; follow the specific notification. [s1] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
Required: junior-level and higher mathematics courses, transcript-matching numbers, topics and textbooks;
identify graduate courses. [s1]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Topics belong in the required mathematics-course list; a separate full syllabus document is not listed. Portal
attachment limits are unverified. [s1]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
At least three; letters must be dated within one year. [s1]

Scholarship references [Standing rule]
University Fellows requires a separate departmental nomination letter; it is not described as a fourth external
referee letter. Its review questions and format differ from admissions letters; see scholarship writing field. [s10]
What sends the invitation [Conflict]
Unresolved for Math: another GradApp department says entering referee emails leads to invitations, while the
Eller guide says links go out after remaining checklist items are completed. Do not assume merely typing a
name immediately sends. Read Math's live portal control before activating it. [s13] [s14]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Shared GradApp instructions allow application submission before letters arrive, but the exact Math invitation
trigger and post-submission receipt rules are not publicly confirmed. [s14]
Receipt confirmation [Unresolved]
GradApp has an application processing checklist. A shared-platform recommendation status view is
documented by other departments; Math-specific receipt display and email confirmation are unverified. [s3]
[s12]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No Math rule found for replacing, updating, or reusing a submitted reference. Ask the graduate coordinator; the
one-year letter-age rule still applies. [s1] [s12]

Academic CV / resume [Unresolved]
Not listed in public Math requirements; portal requirement/optional-upload availability, length, format and
upload-versus-link rule unverified. [s1]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
Required. Faithful paraphrase: explain mathematical interests and reasons for graduate study generally and at
Arizona; describe any research project undertaken. Word/page limit, font and file specifications not published;
submit through GradApp. [s1] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
No separately identified background/personal essay found; do not assume the general GradApp 'personal
statement' wording requires an additional document beyond Math's SOP. Prompt and limits unverified. [s1] [s3]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Include mathematical interests and any research experience in SOP. A separate research-interest essay is not
publicly listed; separate prompt/limit/upload permissions unknown. [s1]
Research proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list [Unresolved]
No separate required item located in the public Math application checklist. Optional submission permission,
exact prompt, limits, format and upload/link preference remain unverified. [s1]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
Required mathematics list as above; no public length/font/file limit or link-instead-of-upload permission found.
[s1]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
University Fellows: department uploads a nomination in Word/PDF, single-spaced, 1-inch margins, 12-point
Calibri, maximum three pages, ideally 200 words per review area; headings match review areas. Faithful
paraphrase of areas: future contributions to the field; collaborative/interdisciplinary experience; scholarly
achievements; transferable skills; contribution to Arizona's public-service/land-grant/HSI mission. This is a
departmental nomination, not a published separate applicant essay. International fee-waiver survey questions
could not be read without its JavaScript form. [s10] [s11]

Other short answers / materials [Unresolved]
No additional public Math short-answer set found. Inspect the actual 2027 GradApp form before drafting to
identify portal-only questions. [s1] [s3]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Conflict]
University-wide AY 2026-27 minimum for a 0.50-FTE graduate assistant is USD 25,654 for nine months;
fiscal-year minimum USD 33,350 is a distinct appointment basis. Neither is a published Fall 2027 Math offer.
Handbook's February 2026 table starts at USD 23,000 and is superseded by the later higher floor. At 0.50 FTE,
base tuition and individual student health premium are covered; mandatory/program/course fees are not
generally covered. University Fellows first year: USD 37,000 (15,000 fall + 15,000 spring + 7,000 summer),
base fall/spring tuition and health; year-two professional-development USD 500. [s5] [s6] [s7] [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Handbook describes support after year three for two, possibly three more years subject to progress and
teaching; sixth-year support needs advisor/committee recommendation and beyond six is exceptional. A
guaranteed initial multi-year 2027 package was not located. University Fellows requires departmental support
in years 2-5, subject to performance and funds, with specified minimum support; first-year award is not the
ordinary TA stipend. [s5] [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International students may pursue departmental assistantships subject to teaching-English and appointment
rules. University Fellows eligibility says any newly admitted qualifying doctoral student, without a citizenship
restriction. Graduate Access Fellowship explicitly targets domestic students and is not an F-1 funding route. [s1]
[s8] [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Assistantship continuation requires satisfactory progress and teaching, at least six credits and GPA 3.0 under
handbook rules. First-year teaching load is four units per semester; later nine annually, plus training. University
Fellows requires full-time nine-credit enrollment, GPA 3.0, cohort participation, and normally no other paid
work in year one; exceptions require approval. [s5] [s9]
Extra funding application [Unresolved]
No separate standard TA application located. University Fellows requires department selection and nomination
(up to two nominees/program). Ask Math early whether it will nominate you; 2027 nomination date is
unpublished. [s1] [s10]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
University Fellows; department awards for enrolled students, including teaching/research awards and some
later-stage university nominations. Math's scholarship page also lists citizenship- or institution-restricted
schemes; Arizona-undergraduate awards and domestic Graduate Access funding do not fit this UChicago F-1
profile. [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 90 central graduate application fee, unless a qualifying program waiver applies; nonrefundable after
payment. [s4]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Math offers international applicants a free prescreen survey for possible fee waiver; apply through the linked
Qualtrics form before paying. Eligibility threshold, survey questions and 2027 cutoff are not publicly readable.
The separate broad domestic waiver is explicitly Fall 2026 and does not establish John's eligibility. Graduate
College does not provide a general waiver for everyone. [s1] [s4] [s11]

Old Math TOEFL scale versus updated central rules; February 2026 handbook stipend below AY 2026-27
university minimum; different departments' GradApp invitation wording. Pure Mathematics must not be
